candidate.educational_objective: Apply healthcare fire-response principles of facility-plan activation, compartmentation, defend-in-place, and targeted relocation.

options.A: Begin immediate building-wide evacuation of all patients regardless of location, because healthcare fire response requires complete evacuation as the first protective action.
options.B: Follow the facility fire-response plan, use compartmentation to defend patients in place when safe, and relocate those in threatened areas as conditions require.
options.C: Keep all patients in their current rooms until the fire department arrives, because compartmentation eliminates the need for relocation during a hospital fire.
options.D: Open corridor doors throughout the unit to improve visibility and movement, then relocate patients before activating the hospital fire-response process.

candidate.rationale: Healthcare occupancies are designed around compartmentation and a defend-in-place strategy rather than automatic whole-building evacuation. Joint Commission fire-safety guidance explains that protected compartments permit patients to remain in safe care areas while threatened patients can be relocated as the fire-response plan requires; full evacuation is a last resort when protection or conditions require it. Staff should follow the organization’s fire-response plan rather than apply a memorized acronym as a universal substitute for the actual emergency plan.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Healthcare fire response relies on the facility plan, compartmentation/defend-in-place, and relocation of threatened occupants rather than automatic total evacuation.
